questions.stem:
What is the objective function in the following linear programming problem?
Maximize: 3x + 4y
Subject to:
x + y ≤ 10
2x - y ≤ 8
x, y ≥ 0
questions.solution: The objective function is the expression that we want to maximize in a linear programming problem. In this case, it is '3x + 4y'. The other expressions are constraints.
questions.explanation: The objective function defines what we want to optimize in a linear programming problem.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake would be to choose one of the constraint inequalities (A or B), which represent the limits on the variables, rather than the actual target to optimize.
